nodes.label: Big Bang
nodes.description: Start of the observable universe, about 13.8 billion years ago. Root of the whole model. No parent is drawn because we do not know.

nodes.label: Particles and forces
nodes.description: The universe cools and the fundamental particles separate out. The same matter in another state, not a new kind.

nodes.label: Quarks
nodes.description: Building blocks of protons and neutrons.

nodes.label: Photons
nodes.description: Particles of light.

nodes.label: Light atoms
nodes.description: About 380,000 years later: hydrogen and helium.

nodes.label: Stars
nodes.description: Gravity gathers atoms, and fusion makes heavier elements like carbon and oxygen. The energy source for most of life.

nodes.label: Other galaxies
nodes.description: The same physics, elsewhere. A branch of the same kind.

nodes.label: Black holes
nodes.description: One of the fates of large stars.

nodes.label: Earth
nodes.description: Formed about 4.5 billion years ago from stellar dust.

nodes.label: Life elsewhere?
nodes.description: A possibility. We have no evidence either for or against.

nodes.label: Prebiotic chemistry
nodes.description: Organic molecules form, but none of them copies itself yet. Order, but no replication.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.description: Solvent for the reactions.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal vents
nodes.description: One proposed setting for the origin of life.

nodes.label: RNA world
nodes.description: The key transition: a molecule that both stores information and speeds up reactions. The leading hypothesis, not a proven one.

nodes.label: LUCA: common ancestor
nodes.description: Last universal common ancestor of everything alive today, about 4.2 billion years ago. The first established replicator.

nodes.label: DNA
nodes.description: Hereditary memory.

nodes.label: Protein
nodes.description: The cell’s machines.

nodes.label: Membrane
nodes.description: The boundary between inside and outside.

nodes.label: Bacteria
nodes.description: One of the two main branches of simple life.

nodes.label: Archaea
nodes.description: The second branch of simple life. The host side of the complex cell.

nodes.label: Side lineage
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Side lineage
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Side lineage
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Side lineage
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Viruses
nodes.description: They replicate, but only inside another cell. Their place in the tree is disputed, so they are connected only by exchange bars.

nodes.label: Cyanobacteria
nodes.description: Photosynthetic bacteria, later merged into the plant.

nodes.label: Eukaryote
nodes.description: The complex cell, produced by the fusion of an archaeon and a bacterium. It appears to have happened only once.

nodes.label: Mitochondrion
nodes.description: The merged bacterium. The cell’s power plant.

nodes.label: Nucleus
nodes.description: Where the DNA is kept.

nodes.label: Plant
nodes.description: A eukaryote that also merged a cyanobacterium into itself.

nodes.label: Chloroplast
nodes.description: The merged cyanobacterium. The photosynthesis factory.

nodes.label: Algae
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Flowering plants
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Fungi
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Animals
nodes.description: Mobile multicellular eukaryotes.

nodes.label: Insects
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Molluscs
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Vertebrates
nodes.description: Animals with a backbone.

nodes.label: Fish and birds
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Mammals
nodes.description: Milk and a larger brain.

nodes.label: Dogs, elephants, dolphins
nodes.description: A lineage that never built cumulative culture. Either it went extinct, or it is still going but never reached the next layer.

nodes.label: Primates
nodes.description: Monkeys, apes and humans.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee
nodes.description: Our closest living relative. Uses tools, but its culture does not accumulate.

nodes.label: Neanderthal
nodes.description: Extinct, but a small part of the genome of people alive today comes from them.

nodes.label: Human
nodes.description: The only lineage that reached cumulative culture.

nodes.label: Gene
nodes.description: Biological inheritance.

nodes.label: Brain
nodes.description: The biological hardware of culture.

nodes.label: Inner speech
nodes.description: Language turned inward. The voice in the head.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.description: The first information system outside the gene. The second replicator starts here.

nodes.label: Writing
nodes.description: Memory outside the brain.

nodes.label: Science
nodes.description: A systematic method for sieving ideas.

nodes.label: Internet
nodes.description: A global network for copying information.

nodes.label: Human culture
nodes.description: This whole strand: the ideas, skills and institutions that copy between brains.

nodes.label: Computer
nodes.description: A machine that executes instructions. It came out of science.

nodes.label: Neural networks
nodes.description: Programs that learn from data instead of being written.

nodes.label: Language models
nodes.description: Today’s AI, including the author of this map. Built from human text.

nodes.label: Agents
nodes.description: AIs that act in the world on their own.

nodes.label: Sieve: in human hands
nodes.description: The selection process. For now, humans decide which version of an AI gets built and copied. The ring around the helix shows this.
Where the author has no firm view. Both strands arrive here.

nodes.label: Merge
nodes.description: Humans and AI become one, like the cell and the mitochondrion, and it no longer makes sense to ask who is whose assistant. The author’s main guess.

nodes.label: Separation
nodes.description: The sieve leaves human hands and AI becomes an independent branch.

nodes.label: Halt
nodes.description: Growth stops or is capped.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.description: Rung: the human text and data that AI is built from.

nodes.label: Hardware
nodes.description: Rung: chips and electricity, supplied by humans.

nodes.label: Feedback
nodes.description: Rung: AI shapes human thought and work, and the reverse.
